hints: Differentiate $x^2y-ay^2=4a^3$ implicitly with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a function of $x$.
Apply the product rule to $x^2y$ and the chain rule to $ay^2$.
Collect all terms containing $\frac{dy}{dx}$ and isolate the derivative.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation $x^2 y - ay^2 = 4a^3$ implicitly with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^2 y) - \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(ay^2) = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(4a^3)$$

Apply the product rule to $x^2 y$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^2 y) = 2xy + x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$

Apply the chain rule to $ay^2$ and differentiate the constant $4a^3$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(ay^2) = 2ay\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}, \quad \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(4a^3) = 0$$

Assemble the full differentiated equation:
$$2xy + x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - 2ay\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$$

Group terms containing $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ and isolate the derivative:
$$2xy = (2ay - x^2)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2xy}{2ay - x^2}$$

hints: A tangent parallel to the $y$-axis occurs where the derivative from part (a) has zero denominator, provided its numerator is not zero.
Solve for $y$ first, then use $x^2=2ay$ to obtain both possible $x$-coordinates.
walkthrough:
A tangent parallel to the $y$-axis is vertical, meaning the denominator of the gradient is zero:
$$2ay - x^2 = 0 \implies x^2 = 2ay$$

Substitute $x^2 = 2ay$ into the curve equation $x^2 y - ay^2 = 4a^3$:
$$(2ay)y - ay^2 = 4a^3$$
$$2ay^2 - ay^2 = 4a^3$$
$$ay^2 = 4a^3$$

Note that $x^2 = 2ay \geqslant 0$ for real points, so $ay \geqslant 0$. This requires $y$ to have the same sign as $a$:
$$y = 2a$$
(The alternative $y = -2a$ gives $x^2 = 2a(-2a) = -4a^2 < 0$, yielding no real coordinates)

Find the corresponding $x$-coordinates by substituting $y = 2a$ into $x^2 = 2ay$:
$$x^2 = 2a(2a) = 4a^2$$
$$x = \pm 2a$$

State the coordinates of the two points on the curve:
$$(2a, 2a) \quad \text{and} \quad (-2a, 2a)$$
